20208-boy-scouts-in-the-philippines-or-t:
Boy Scouts in the Philippines, from 1911, sends its troop across the Pacific. Frank means to sleep again aboard ship but fails at once. Jimmie grabs him by the shoulders and dumps him on a scarlet rug. The rug covers the floor of their shared stateroom at sea.

Horseplay soon gives way to the key to the treaty box. That object drives the plot once the boys reach the islands. Scout tales of this era mix travel, teamwork, and patriotic missions. Readers get a lively trip to the Philippines as Americans then pictured it.
22106-john-knox:
John Knox, the thundering preacher who remade Scotland's church, is the subject of this biography. Knox spent years in exile and in a French galley before his hour came. The writer compares him to the old prophets who waited in the desert. Like them, Knox was hidden until the day of his showing to his people.

The life follows his preaching, his clashes with Mary Queen of Scots, and the building of the Reformed Kirk. Knox's rough spear-head manner gets full credit for breaking Rome's hold on Scotland. This account treats him as a hero of faith and nation. It shows the place Knox still held in Protestant memory centuries after his death.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-charles-antoi: A 1913 entry on Coysevox — the sculptor of the Sun King's marble. Marie Louise Handley honors his Versailles works. His busts crowned the great gallery. The Louvre keeps his mighty tombs. The master of the French chisel. His Marly horses are famed.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-john-knox: This 1913 reference article on Knox — the Scottish reformer. Oswald Hunter-Blair unfolds his fateful sway. His voice toppled the ancient altars. The age knew the thundering name. The sixteenth century told his tale. His 1572 death is famed. His 1560 reform is famed.
lady-into-fox:
David Garnett published Lady into Fox in October 1922. Wood engravings by R. A. Garnett illustrate it. Garnett opens by noting that marvels come in uneven crops across the centuries.

His marvel is simple and strange: Mrs. Tebrick turns into a fox. Her husband must face life with a wife who is now an animal. Garnett tells the change in calm, plain prose. That calm makes each new loss feel sharper. The short novel became a quiet classic of English fantasy. The wood engravings add a storybook feel to a sad tale. Garnett keeps the ending quiet rather than spectacular.
longstreet-manassas-appomattox:
James Longstreet, Lee's senior corps commander, published From Manassas to Appomattox in 1896. Southern critics had blamed Longstreet for the loss at Gettysburg, and he wrote to defend himself. Lee had called him his Old War Horse.

Longstreet narrates the eastern war from First Manassas to the surrender, with maps and frank judgments. He defends his moves at Gettysburg and faults others, including Lee's plan there. His friendship with Grant, his old army comrade, colors the closing chapters. The memoir is key, and contested, evidence on how the Confederacy lost its greatest battles. Maps and returns from his own files back many of his claims.
nasa-tm-19670030753-a-resonance-tube-ign:
E. William Conrad and Albert J. Pavli, of NASA's Lewis Research Center in Cleveland, report a flameless lighter for rockets in this October 1967 memorandum. The device is a resonance-tube igniter for hydrogen-oxygen engines. A resonance tube heats gas at its closed end through pressure waves alone, with no spark.

The authors studied the resonance effects and tuned them using a burning mixture ratio of hydrogen and oxygen. Their data show how the tube's geometry changes the temperature reached at the cavity bottom. That peak heat proved enough to ignite the mixture. The test demonstrated that a resonance tube can serve as an igniter.
nasa-tm-19720024159-apollo-16-mission-an:
Apollo 16 flew in 1972, and this report deals with a failure found after the mission. The Mission Evaluation Team at Houston prepared it in June 1972. Owen G. Morris, manager of the Apollo Spacecraft Program, approved it. Its subject is a tank used while draining oxidizer from the command module.

Ground crews emptied leftover propellant from the reaction control system after flight. Their gear was built to make the propellant safe, in both liquid and gas form, before disposal. The report records what went wrong with the oxidizer tank during that work. Such reports helped NASA fix faults before later flights.
old-granny-fox:
Thornton Waldo Burgess wrote this animal story for children. Granny Fox and Reddy Fox hunt through a hard winter. Snow covers the meadows, and ice binds the pool. Food is scarce, so they hunt almost all day. Farmer Brown's boy and Bowser the Hound threaten them.

The contents list traps, storms, and a midnight hen hunt. Granny admits she is growing old and slower. Reddy learns respect for her wisdom and skill. Burgess teaches nature lore through each small adventure. Gentle morals close the tales of the Green Forest. Winter hunger makes each small choice matter for the foxes' survival.
reynard-the-fox: Reynard the Fox, John Masefield's verse epic. The trickster fox. This book preserves that poem. The file is now open to the public. Its contents inform the historical record. The library keeps the document safe.
the-adventure-of-the-cardboard-box: A Sherlock Holmes story about a cardboard box containing two severed ears: the lonely Miss Cushing's grim parcel. Holmes traces it to a tragedy of jealousy. One of the grimmest of the canon. The Crocker case is among Holmes's darkest.
the-adventures-of-reddy-fox: Thornton Burgess's beloved children's book about Reddy Fox, the sly young fox of the Green Meadows, and his scrapes with Farmer Brown's boy and Reddy's enemies. Gentle morals and animal lore fill these nature stories. A childhood classic of the American outdoors.
the-man-on-the-box: Harold MacGrath's sparkling comedy of errors was a stage and screen hit before it was a beloved novel. A young man-about-town is mistaken for a coachman and decides to play along — with romantic complications, of course. Light, fast, and full of charm, it is early-twentieth-century romantic comedy at its most effervescent.
the-man-who-kept-his-money-in-a-box: Trollope's The Man Who Kept His Money in a Box is a comic travel tale. An Englishman guards his cashbox across the Continent with absurd care. Mishaps multiply at every border. A delightful minor Trollope.
the-silver-box: The Silver Box, John Galsworthy's play. The stolen purse. This book preserves that drama. Its pages add to the record of the past. Scholars prize such firsthand sources. The paper lived through the years. Writers of history may cite it later in their work.
the-wrong-box: Stevenson and Lloyd Osbourne's 1889 farce about a tontine, a corpse in a barrel, and uncles who won't die on schedule. Mistaken bodies pile up in this black comedy of inheritance. The funniest book Stevenson ever wrote.
